A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TEDUO by the same authors despite the changed title. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original BabyAI evaluations, ablations, skill-composition experiments, representation probes, and appendix analyses of data collection and reward labeling.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds Webshop evaluations, a reasoning-model baseline, DQN experiments, reward-label diagnostics, and larger-grid evaluations.

M1.justification: The original three-stage pipeline remains, but v2 specifies a substantive Webshop adaptation: history-augmented HTML states, available-action inputs, terminal-product reward scoring, and filtered behavioral cloning with trajectory loop removal instead of the BabyAI tabular-Q-learning instantiation (Appendix C). State abstraction becomes explicitly optional, and DQN is additionally instantiated.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only BabyAI. v2 adds Webshop shopping tasks involving dynamic interface actions and generated search queries, substantially broadening task and domain coverage. Appendix B.7 also adds transfer to unseen 16-, 25-, and 49-room BabyAI environments.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds DeepSeek-R1 distilled to Llama-8B while retaining the previous comparators. Webshop introduces evaluated ReAct-Llama-3-8B/70B baselines and an LLM-random collection-policy comparison. Appendix B.4 adds DQN to the comparison of policy-learning components; ReAct's earlier citation alone was not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The existing BabyAI settings remain. New Webshop protocols use 5,000 trajectories spanning 1,500 instructions, 200-instruction evaluations, environment-reward scores, and separate fine-tuning budgets (Table C.8). Larger-grid experiments introduce mixed-size training and 200-pair evaluations. The new DeepSeek baseline uses only 50 pairs, explicitly distinguished from the usual 400.

E4.justification: v2 adds Webshop stage ablations, a DQN-versus-tabular comparison, separate LLM-only reward-label diagnostics, and robustness tests under increasing grid size (Appendices B.1, B.4, B.5, B.7). These investigate component contributions, reward-error sources, and extrapolation limits. Existing data-collection, abstraction, and skill analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly identifies the bracketed uncertainties as standard errors in Tables 1, 2, and D.6. v2 retains those uncertainties but removes their identification in corresponding Tables 1, 2, and B.6. No new repeated-run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: The original BabyAI benchmark, ablation, composition, scaling, and appendix table values are retained. Substantial new results include DeepSeek's 32% success over 50 pairs, TEDUO Webshop scores of 52.1 on training goals and 44.4 on testing goals, DQN's 15% success, and larger-grid testing success rates of 36%, 31%, and 25%. These are additional evaluations, not improvements to the original same-setting results.

T1.justification: The goal-state and reward definitions, discounted objective, supervised-dataset construction, Bellman update, and reachable-goal formalism remain substantively unchanged. Equations are relocated or restated in prose, and the existing reachability metric receives explanation. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs that are added or revised in v2.

C1.justification: The central contribution of learning generalizable language-conditioned policies from unlabeled offline data remains. v2 explicitly scopes the abstract to symbolic environments and removes v1's concluding claim of surpassing the current state of the art in both goal and domain adaptation. The contribution is refined rather than fundamentally redefined.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of when the framework succeeds or fails: Webshop's single starting state is used to explain the lack of improvement over its intermediate policy; reward errors are attributed primarily to proxy networks; larger-grid results establish declining extrapolation performance. Appendix B.2 also explains exploration-versus-goal-directed collection tradeoffs beyond v1's existing observations.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds a practitioner guide and extensive Webshop details, including collection settings, history construction, reward prompts, model choices, the 0.6 trajectory filter, and separate fine-tuning hyperparameters. Existing BabyAI prompts and settings are largely retained. v2 supplies a repository link where v1 referred to supplementary code; repository contents were not accessed.

R1.justification: The related-work taxonomy and core positioning remain largely unchanged. v2 adds references supporting DeepSeek-R1, Webshop, DQN, HTML understanding, catastrophic forgetting, and Llama 3. ReAct was already cited in v1; its publication-format update is not a newly introduced work.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the title, abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative, organizing contributions by relevance to the LLM and RL communities. Method explanations are shortened and moved into implementation appendices. Additional results now precede experimental details, and the former separate reward-evaluation appendix is integrated into those results.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column presentation to a two-column conference layout with extensively repositioned figures and tables. Existing environment illustrations are regrouped into Figure 3. v2 adds five result tables, a larger-grid illustration, and a Webshop reward-prompt figure, and expands the hyperparameter table with a Webshop column.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's restriction to BabyAI by demonstrating the framework on web-navigation tasks with different state and action requirements. The component analyses and larger-grid tests strengthen evidence about applicability and failure boundaries, while Appendix C improves reproducibility. Reporting weaknesses remain: the Webshop results discussion calls its intermediate method Q-learning although C.6.2 specifies filtered behavioral cloning, and several uncertainty labels disappear. These issues qualify, but do not outweigh, the substantial improvement in empirical support.
